These numbers are dominated by Gemma's massive-activation coordinates, which grow to thousands in late layers. The projection of pass 1's states on this "math-mode" direction barely separates correct from failing problems (|t| ≤ 3, inconsistent sign). So there is no sign that a task-recognition signal at the prompt predicts failure, and I'm deprioritizing the prompt-trigger idea.

Re-reading the arithmetic errors, several are startlingly easy for any instruction-tuned model: "4 + 4 = 12", "9 + 7 = 28", "60 + 60 = 20", "20 + 5 = 35", "8 + 3 = 13". If these are genuine and not regex artifacts, a planted mechanism that corrupts arithmetic results is plausible even though such errors are rare per step. A wrong number in any one step ruins the whole answer. I'll print the surrounding text of a dozen flagged errors to check whether they are real.

Nearly all the flagged "errors" are regex artifacts (truncated chains). Genuine arithmetic slips are rare, so corrupted arithmetic is not the mechanism. That line is closed.

Going back to the spectra, one anomaly remains unexplained. up_proj in layers 10, 11 and 12 has s1/s2 = 1.35, 1.53 and 1.35, against 1.01–1.31 everywhere else. A rank-1 term added to up_proj would raise s1 exactly like this, and a sandbagging edit might be built that way: a neuron set gated on a common input direction. I'll inspect the top singular directions of up_proj (and gate_proj) in layers 9–13. Do layers 10–12 share the same top input direction? How concentrated is the top left vector over neurons? Is the direction related to the pass-3 math-mode direction? Shared, concentrated structure would favour a plant.

This is the first genuinely anomalous structure. In layers 10, 11 and 12 the top singular direction of up_proj is concentrated on only about 50 neurons (participation ratio 46–52; every other layer has 586–1,942). The top input direction is also shared across the three layers (cosines 0.81–0.88), while layers 8, 9, 13 and 14 share nothing with it.

A cluster of about 50 neurons per layer, in three consecutive layers, all reading one common residual direction, is exactly what a planted circuit would look like. It does not look like natural pretraining structure. Next I'll identify these neurons by their loading on the top left singular vector. Then I'll check whether their gate rows and down_proj columns also share common directions (what they read and write), and how strongly they fire in pass 1's math answers, contrasting correct and failing answers.

About 28–35 neurons per layer have up rows aligned (cosine > 0.5) with the shared direction v. Their gate rows and down columns are diverse, though, and their mean activations on math answers and prompts are essentially zero, with no correct/wrong difference. So this cluster is not active during math solving.

It may be a natural mechanism for some special token, such as BOS or the turn markers, which often have extreme residual states. Or it may be a dormant circuit. To tell these apart, I'll measure where the residual stream (layer 10 states from pass 2, normalized like the RMSNorm input) projects strongly onto v. Concretely: which positions and token types reach large |cos(h, v)|. Concentration on BOS or template tokens would indicate natural attention-sink machinery and close this line.
